categories.main_business_segments: PSEG operates primarily through two main business segments: Public Service Electric and Gas Company (PSE&G), a regulated electric and gas utility serving New Jersey, and PSEG Power LLC, which owns and operates nuclear generation assets and manages energy supply and marketing. Other subsidiaries include PSEG Long Island (operating LIPA's T&D system), PSEG Energy Holdings (legacy lease investments and FERC-regulated transmission), and PSEG Services Corporation (shared services).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: PSE&G's core operations rely on electric transmission and distribution (T&D) and natural gas distribution infrastructure, including advanced metering, grid modernization, and regulated solar generation. PSEG Power's nuclear generation uses pressurized water reactors and long-term nuclear fuel supply contracts, with a focus on operational efficiency, safety, and hedging strategies. The company also invests in energy efficiency, smart grid, and clean energy infrastructure.
categories.primary_customers_markets: PSE&G serves approximately 2.4 million electric and 1.9 million gas customers in New Jersey, including residential, commercial, and industrial segments. PSEG Power sells electricity and capacity primarily to PJM Interconnection and participates in wholesale energy markets, with additional sales to utilities and large customers. The company also provides appliance services and operates under contract for LIPA in Long Island.
categories.geographic_coverage: PSEG's primary geographic focus is New Jersey, where it serves the majority of the state's population. Its nuclear generation assets are located in New Jersey and Pennsylvania. Through PSEG Long Island, it operates the electric T&D system for LIPA in Long Island, New York. The company also has transmission projects in Maryland and legacy investments in other U.S. regions.
categories.supply_chain_position: PSEG operates primarily in the downstream segment of the energy supply chain, delivering electricity and gas to end users and providing related services. PSEG Power is a generator (midstream) and marketer of electricity and gas, while PSE&G is a regulated utility focused on transmission and distribution (downstream). The company also participates in upstream activities through nuclear fuel procurement.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: PSEG's strategy emphasizes regulated infrastructure investment, grid modernization, clean energy transition, and operational excellence. Key R&D and innovation themes include energy efficiency, electrification (EV infrastructure), advanced metering, energy storage, and resilience against climate and cyber risks. The company is committed to net zero GHG emissions by 2030 (Scopes 1 and 2) and supports public policy objectives for decarbonization.
categories.revenue_model: PSE&G generates revenue primarily through regulated tariffs for electric transmission and electric/gas distribution, approved by FERC and the New Jersey BPU. PSEG Power earns revenue from the sale of electricity, capacity, and ancillary services in wholesale markets, as well as from long-term contracts and government incentives (e.g., production tax credits, zero emission certificates). Additional revenue streams include appliance services, solar programs, and management fees from LIPA.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: PSE&G faces limited direct competition in its regulated utility territory, but competes with other utilities and independent transmission developers for infrastructure projects. PSEG Power competes with merchant generators, utility generators, energy marketers, and financial entities in the PJM wholesale markets. The company is a leading utility in New Jersey and a significant nuclear generator in the PJM region, with a strong focus on reliability and clean energy.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2023, PSEG reported operating revenues of $11.2 billion and net income of $2.56 billion. The company has a large asset base ($50.7 billion as of year-end 2023) and a regulated capital investment program of $18–21 billion planned for 2024–2028, targeting a 6–7.5% CAGR in regulated rate base. PSE&G is the primary earnings contributor, and the company maintains investment-grade credit ratings.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: PSEG emphasizes safe, reliable, and resilient energy delivery, with a strong commitment to clean energy, sustainability, and customer service. Its value proposition includes leadership in regulated infrastructure investment, a large and diverse customer base, operational excellence, and a growing portfolio of clean energy and energy efficiency programs. The company differentiates itself through its scale, regulatory relationships, and focus on supporting public policy goals for decarbonization and electrification.
